title: Choose jobdeck's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Registry. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Registry
options.lineage: npm / crates.io package pages, lockfiles, dependency trees
options.thesis: Every job is a package: skills are its dependencies, and your resume will be the lockfile it resolves against.
materials: frosted glass panes over a dark ink field
options.viewport: Search bar as a registry query; left rail of facets as package filters; dense result rows reading like `company / title@seniority`, skills as dependency chips, salary and age in tabular mono; glass detail pane opens on the right as the package page.
options.risk: Metaphor can turn cute if package jargon leaks into labels; it must stay structural, not wordplay.

raised.raise: Rows rerank in place: when a filter or sort changes, rows slide to their new position instead of re-rendering, and new-since-last-visit rows hold an amber mark until seen.
Numbers are one tabular mono column grid; the selected row inverts instead of getting a soft highlight.
One visible 4px-based column grid shared by rail, list and pane; every cell snaps to it.
List rank is carried by weight and color, never by size: one type size across the whole result list.

options.label: The Command Palette
options.lineage: Spotlight, Raycast, VS Code quick open
options.thesis: The whole app is one floating glass palette: type, filter with tokens, arrow, enter.
options.viewport: A centered glass palette over a blurred field; filters typed as tokens (role:backend remote:global); results stream below; detail expands inline.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most dev-tool UIs land, and dense facet counts have nowhere to live.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: airport gate boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: Fresh roles depart in posting order; the board reranks live and a changed row holds its alert color.
options.viewport: Full-width board of rows in fixed columns (time, company, role, region, pay); the opened job renders as a segmented pass.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on clarity (recency ordering is exactly triage) but developers don't identify with travel; loses on audience.
options.risk: Novelty board look fights the glass brief.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Jobs as a strobing black-and-white data field.
options.viewport: Barcode columns per role family with numbers packed in margins.
options.case: Fuses poorly: pure spectacle obscures the reading task and drops the pinned glass material.
options.kept: Selection by inversion and strictly tabular mono numerics.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The layout grid is the design.
options.viewport: Monumental grid letterforms over a small grotesk list.
options.case: Fuses poorly: display letterforms have no job in a triage tool.
options.kept: One visible grid shared by every region.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and rule.
options.viewport: Raked glass slides on a lit goldenrod bed.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the 11-degree rake costs scanning speed.
options.risk: Raked rows are slower to read.
options.kept: One type size in the list; rank by weight and color.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One plant through its seasons at fixed scale.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no developer identification, no triage task.
options.kept: Fixed-scale comparability: every row shows the same fields in the same cells.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: Companies as a ranked mascot roster.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful register contradicts the minimal, dev-centric brief.
options.kept: Each entry keeps its fixed furniture in fixed cells.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean job board: filter sidebar, card list, job page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Left filters, cards with logo/title/location/salary, detail on its own page.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from LinkedIn/Indeed by design; drops the glass brief.
